claims.text: Issue #1241 concerns validity checks on match indices against the compressor window's lowLimit, where an index is considered valid only if it is >= lowLimit ("below that point, no more data").

The code enforces "a simple check that index >= lowLimit to see if index is valid" and clamps nextToUpdate up to window.lowLimit, showing that a lowLimit of 0 on first usage of context would make index 0 appear invalid/edge-case problematic.

Window bounds are initialized/maintained via ZSTD_window_init (window->lowLimit = end) and correction updates, so on first usage the starting lowLimit value determines whether the first input position (index 0 vs 1) passes validity checks for a match.

ZSTD_window_update() sets window->dictLimit = (U32)(window->nextSrc - window->base) when a non-contiguous segment starts, so at the very first usage the base/nextSrc delta is 0, meaning indices/positions start at 0. A first input position of 0 (index 0) can therefore be produced, which the fix (starting reference at 1) avoids; ZSTD_window_enforceMaxDist() computes current = srcEnd - window->base from this same base, so the position validity checks (index >= lowLimit) operate on the same 0-origin indexing."}]}

claims.text: The reference position is tracked via the window state (lowLimit/dictLimit/base) in ZSTD_window_t. ZSTD_window_update() sets window->dictLimit = (U32)(window->nextSrc - window->base) when a non-contiguous segment starts, so at the very first usage the base/nextSrc delta is 0, meaning indices/positions start at 0. A first input position of 0 (index 0) can therefore be produced, which the fix (starting reference at 1) avoids; ZSTD_window_enforceMaxDist() computes current = srcEnd - window->base from this same base, so the position validity checks (index >= lowLimit) operate on the same 0-origin indexing.

claims.text: Issue #1241 concerns validity checks on match indices against the compressor window's lowLimit, where an index is considered valid only if it is >= lowLimit ("below that point, no more data").

The code enforces "a simple check that index >= lowLimit to see if index is valid" and clamps nextToUpdate up to window.lowLimit, showing that a lowLimit of 0 on first usage of context would make index 0 appear invalid/edge-case problematic.

Window bounds are initialized/maintained via ZSTD_window_init (window->lowLimit = end) and correction updates, so on first usage the starting lowLimit value determines whether the first input position (index 0 vs 1) passes validity checks for a match.

The reference position is tracked via the window state (lowLimit/dictLimit/base) in ZSTD_window_t. ZSTD_window_update() sets window->dictLimit = (U32)(window->nextSrc - window->base) when a non-contiguous segment starts, so at the very first usage the base/nextSrc delta is 0, meaning indices/positions start at 0. A first input position of 0 (index 0) can therefore be produced, which the fix (starting reference at 1) avoids; ZSTD_window_enforceMaxDist() computes current = srcEnd - window->base from this same base, so the position validity checks (index >= lowLimit) operate on the same 0-origin indexing.
